member.name: T:ReactiveUI.TransitioningContentControl
member.summary: A that animates the visual transition whenever its changes.

remarks.para: works by taking a bitmap “snapshot” of the previously displayed content (rendered to a ) and then running a WPF transition between that image and the new content.
The default template is expected to define the following named parts:

item.description: PART_Container: a (typically a ) that hosts visual states.
PART_PreviousImageSite: an used to display a snapshot of the outgoing content.
PART_CurrentContentPresentationSite: a used to display the incoming content.
When changes, the control captures a bitmap snapshot of the current visual from PART_CurrentContentPresentationSite into PART_PreviousImageSite.
The new content is assigned to PART_CurrentContentPresentationSite.
A associated with the configured visual state is started using .
When the transition completes, the control returns to the Normal state and clears the outgoing snapshot image.

remarks.para: Most transitions use the visual state name Transition_{Transition}{Direction}. For example: Transition_SlideLeft.
uses Transition_Fade (no direction suffix).
uses a two-phase animation: an “out” phase followed by an “in” phase: Transition_Bounce{Direction}Out then Transition_Bounce{Direction}In.

The event fires after a transition has been queued and just before the first visual state is entered. The event fires after the storyboard completes and the control has returned to Normal (and released the outgoing snapshot image).

item.description: If the template has not been applied yet (for example, prior to ), the control falls back to simply updating the content with no animation.
If a transition is already in progress, additional content changes update the current content immediately (no queued animations).

Snapshot creation depends on the element’s current layout size. If the content presenter has a zero width or height, the snapshot is not meaningful and the control will effectively behave like a normal .
